    Compute survival analysis using CoxPH and Kaplan-Meier Models

    compute.survival.analysis.Rd

    This function performs survival analysis by fitting univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) models on combinations of the input features. It uses the linear predictors from the CoxPH model to stratify patients into high- and low-risk groups based on a threshold (default the median). Kaplan-Meier survival curves are then generated for each group, and a log-rank test is performed to assess statistical significance. Survival curves are saved as PDF files under the Results/ directory.

    compute.survival.analysis(
  features,
  survival.data,
  time_unit,
  p.value = 0.05,
  thres = 0.5,
  max_factors = Inf
)

    Arguments

    features

    A numeric matrix or data frame of cell group or module scores. Rows correspond to samples and columns to different features.

    survival.data

    A data frame containing survival information. Must include:

    PFS_Days

    Numeric vector of progression-free survival times.

    PFS_Outcome

    Binary vector (0/1) indicating progression/recurrence/death (1 = event, 0 = censored).

    time_unit

    A string indicating the time unit used in survival analysis (e.g., "days", "months", "years"). This is used for x-axis labeling in Kaplan-Meier plots.

    p.value

    Significance threshold for the log-rank test p-value. Only combinations with p-value below this threshold will be considered significant. Default is 0.05.

    thres

    Threshold used to binarize the risk scores into high and low groups. Default is 0.5, corresponding to the median.

    max_factors

    Maximum number of features to include in a model. Default is Inf, meaning all combinations will be considered.

    Value

    A named list of significant model formulas (as formula objects), with corresponding Kaplan-Meier plots saved as PDFs in the Results/ folder.
